mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the monthly CPIAUCSL inflation index above 0.3% in a month coincides with a 20-day positive S&P 500 forward return, reflecting market anticipation of rate cuts by the Federal Reserve.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 0.3% in a given month
failure_condition: Over 60-day rolling window, 20-day forward returns do not outperform a 0.2% inflation baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or CPIAUCSL does not exceed 0.3% in any subsequent month for 6 months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly rise in PAYEMS labor cost index exceeding 0.5% is associated with negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns, as higher wage growth is interpreted as a labor-market tightening that dampens equity valuation multiples.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by more than 0.5% month-over-month
failure_condition: In regimes where PAYEMS rises ≤ 0.5% monthly, the 20-day forward return is not statistically different from zero (IC > 0.05), or the effect is reversed in a wage-stagnant environment.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in HOUST retail sales of at least 2% followed by a rebound above the prior month's low predicts a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return, reflecting expectations of improving consumer demand.
candidate_trigger: HOUST falls ≥ 2% in two consecutive months and then rebounds in the third month
failure_condition: Over 12-month windows, the 60-day forward return pattern is not observed when the two-step decline/rebound pattern is absent (IC > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in INDPRO manufacturing index of at least 3% for three consecutive months indicates supply-side weakness, which is associated with negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns as investors anticipate slower growth.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls ≥ 3% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: In periods where INDPRO declines < 3% monthly or not consecutively, the 20-day forward return is not significantly negative (IC > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS rises above 4.5% for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 60-day forward return tends to be negative due to expectations of tighter policy and reduced risk appetite.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by more than 0.5% in two consecutive months
failure_condition: During similar FEDFUNDS moves but in non-tightening regimes (e.g., prior to a Fed hike), the 60-day forward return is not significantly negative (IC > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly rise in both UNRATE unemployment rate and a decline in PAYEMS labor costs by ≥ 0.2% signals a softening labor market, which predicts a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as equities benefit from wage deflation expectations.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE increases while PAYEMS decreases by ≥ 0.2% in the same month
failure_condition: The interaction is not statistically significant (IC > 0.10) in regimes where UNRATE rises and PAYEMS does not fall, or the effect reverses when both proxies move in the opposite direction.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-time drop in GDPC1 personal consumption expenditures (≥ 2% month-over-month) followed by two consecutive months of flat or rising values predicts a positive 5-day S&P 500 forward return as market anticipates stabilization in demand.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls by ≥ 2% in a single month and remains flat or rises in the next two months
failure_condition: The 5-day forward return is not positive when the pattern is absent (IC > 0.15) or the drop is < 2%.

mechanism_narrative: When RSAFS industrial production (demand side proxy) falls by at least 1% for two consecutive months in a row, the S&P 20-day forward return tends to be negative due to persistent supply-side weakness, even if overall GDP growth remains stable.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS decreases by ≥ 1% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: In periods where RSAFS declines < 1% monthly or not consecutively, the 20-day forward return is not significantly negative (IC > 0.10).
